title: FDA 180-Day Generic Exclusivity: Mechanics, Forfeiture, and Shared Exclusivity in Recent First-Generic ANDA Approvals
summary: How FDA's 180-day generic exclusivity is earned, triggered, forfeited, and shared, illustrated by recent first-generic ANDA approvals.
body_markdown:
## FDA 180-day generic exclusivity: how it works, and what recent first-generic ANDAs reveal about forfeiture and shared exclusivity


The 180-day exclusivity incentive is the central reward in the Hatch-Waxman generic system. It gives the first generic applicant to challenge a brand patent a half-year head start against other generics of the same drug. In practice, whether a company actually captures that window turns less on being first and more on avoiding the forfeiture traps written into the statute, and increasingly on sharing the prize with a crowd of same-day filers. Recent first-generic ANDA approvals show both dynamics playing out.


### The core mechanic: first applicant, Paragraph IV, and a 180-day head start


Eligibility begins with a Paragraph IV certification. When a generic applicant submits an ANDA asserting that a patent listed in the Orange Book for the reference product is invalid, unenforceable, or will not be infringed, it opens the door to 180-day exclusivity. The reward goes to the "first applicant," which FDA defines in its approval letters as the applicant that submits a substantially complete ANDA containing a Paragraph IV certification on the first day any such application is submitted for that drug[8](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=8)[10](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=10)[11](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=11) . FDA has restated this test consistently across products such as Sodium Oxybate Oral Solution (ANDA 202090) and Solifenacin Succinate Tablets (ANDA 091464, Teva)[10](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=10)[25](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=25) .


Two features of the test matter for strategy. First, it is a first-day test, not a strict single-winner race: if more than one applicant files a substantially complete Paragraph IV ANDA on that same first day, first-applicant status is shared among them[8](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=8)[53](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=53) . Second, the applicant must be substantially complete on day one; a later-perfected application does not reach back to claim the first-day slot.


The commercial value of first-applicant status is protected by how FDA sequences approvals. Until the 180-day period has "expired, been extinguished, or been relinquished," FDA will not grant final approval to a later generic of the same drug, and CDER's review-prioritization policy is calibrated around that same window[1](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=1) . The 180 days themselves run from the earlier of the first applicant's first commercial marketing or, in some cases, a court decision on the challenged patent.


### Forfeiture: being first is not the same as keeping it


The 2003 Medicare Modernization Act rewrote the exclusivity provision to add forfeiture events precisely because "parked" exclusivity was blocking downstream generics indefinitely. Under section 505(j)(5)(D), a first applicant forfeits exclusivity if any of the enumerated events occurs. FDA's ANDA review memoranda summarize the operative ones: failure to market (the applicant must begin commercial marketing within 75 days of defined triggering events), withdrawal of the application or of the Paragraph IV certification, an agreement with another applicant or the NDA/patent holder found to violate the antitrust laws, expiration of all the challenged patents, and failure to obtain tentative approval within the statutory period[28](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=28) .


In day-to-day practice, the failure-to-obtain-tentative-approval event dominates. Across a long run of approval letters, FDA's stock finding is that the first applicant "failed to obtain tentative approval of this ANDA within 30 months after the date on which the ANDA was filed," citing section 505(j)(5)(D)(i)(IV)[29](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=29)[32](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=32)[35](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=35)[36](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=36)[42](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=42)[43](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=43) . (The clock is 30 months for pre-FDASIA filings and, for later applications, the 30-month figure is adjusted; FDA has applied a 36-month period in at least one case, Dasatinib Tablets ANDA 202103 (Apotex)[14](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=14) .) The consequence is that a company can win the first-to-file race, spend years first in line, and still forfeit the reward simply because its own application was not clean enough to reach tentative approval inside the window.


Recent examples where FDA recorded this tentative-approval forfeiture event in the approval letter include:


Drug product ANDA Applicant Letter date Forfeiture basis cited


Tasimelteon Capsules, 20 mg 211601 Teva 2022-12-12 Failed to obtain tentative approval within 30 months[32](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=32)


Bendamustine HCl for Injection 205376 Dr. Reddy's 2022-12-07 Failed to obtain tentative approval within 30 months[43](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=43)


Mirabegron ER Tablets, 25/50 mg 209485 Lupin 2022-09-28 Failed to obtain tentative approval within 30 months[42](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=42)


Linagliptin Tablets, 5 mg 208335 Sunshine 2021-08-31 Failed to obtain tentative approval within 30 months[35](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=35)


Dimethyl Fumarate DR Capsules 210531 Mylan 2020-08-17 Failed to obtain tentative approval within 30 months[36](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=36)


Asenapine Sublingual Tablets, 10 mg 205960 Breckenridge 2020-12-10 Failed to obtain tentative approval within 30 months[40](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=40)


Naftifine HCl Gel, 2% 208201 Taro 2019-04-10 Failed to obtain tentative approval within 30 months[39](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=39)


The 30-month event is not automatic, though. FDA looks at causation. For Sodium Sulfate, Potassium Sulfate, and Magnesium Sulfate Oral Solution (ANDA 202511), the first applicant missed tentative approval within the period, but FDA found the delay was caused by a change in or review of the approval requirements, and so declined to treat it as a forfeiture[37](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=37)[38](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=38) . FDA reached a similar no-forfeiture conclusion for Clofarabine Injection (ANDA 204029, Abon), noting the applicant was not tentatively approved within 30 months but did not forfeit[12](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=12) . These decisions show the statutory carve-outs are real and fact-specific, not a formality.


The starkest cautionary tale is Ibuprofen Lysine Injection (ANDA 202402): the applicant was "the first ANDA applicant to submit a substantially complete ANDA with a paragraph IV certification," yet FDA's letter recorded that it "failed to obtain tentative approval" within the statutory period, so the first-mover position translated into no exclusivity at all[9](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=9) .


### Shared exclusivity: the 180 days increasingly belong to a crowd


Because the trigger is a first-day test rather than a sole-winner race, multiple companies routinely qualify as co-first applicants and share a single 180-day period. FDA describes this as "shared" 180-day exclusivity: the eligible first applicants share one period, FDA may approve any ANDA that is itself eligible for the exclusivity, and the clock is triggered by the earliest first commercial marketing by any of them (or by a qualifying court decision)[13](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=13)[53](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=53)[57](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=57) .


Two structures recur. In the first, different applicants are "first" on different Orange Book patents, and they share the resulting period, as FDA laid out in the Ribavirin/Ribasphere exclusivity letters, where one applicant was first on one set of patents and another was first on a different set[7](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=7)[48](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=48) . In the second, and now more common, structure, several applicants file substantially complete Paragraph IV ANDAs on the very same first day and become co-first applicants. FDA applied that reasoning to Tranexamic Acid Tablets, 650 mg, where Watson (ANDA 202093) and Apotex (ANDA 202286) both transmitted their Paragraph IV amendments the same day and FDA treated them as co-first applicants sharing the period[8](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=8)[56](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=56)[61](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=61) .


The most recent first-generic approvals show shared exclusivity at scale, and can be seen directly in the Orange Book, where the 180-day patent-challenge exclusivity is coded "PC" and every co-first applicant carries the same expiration date:


- Dapagliflozin (Farxiga) and Dapagliflozin/Metformin (Xigduo XR): FDA approved a large field of first-generic ANDAs on the same day, 2026-04-06, each carrying a PC exclusivity expiring 2026-10-03. The single-agent cohort alone includes Alembic, Alkem, Teva, Sandoz, Biocon, Micro Labs, Ajanta, Inventia, Aizant, and MSN[79](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=79)[80](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=80)[81](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=81)[82](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=82)[83](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=83)[84](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=84)[85](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=85)[86](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=86)[87](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=87) , with Alkem, Sun, and MSN also sharing the combination-product exclusivity[76](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=76)[77](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=77)[78](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=78) . This is shared exclusivity spread across roughly a dozen co-first applicants.
- Sitagliptin (Januvia) and Sitagliptin/Metformin (Janumet): Apotex (ANDA 202425, approved 2026-01-20) and Sandoz (ANDA 202387, approved 2026-01-14) each hold a sitagliptin PC exclusivity expiring 2026-11-24, with Sandoz also carrying the combination exclusivity (ANDA 202388) to the same date[63](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=63)[64](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=64)[67](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=67) .
- Macitentan (Opsumit): Zydus, Teva, Laurus, and Seasons Biotechnology each hold a PC exclusivity expiring 2026-12-03 on their macitentan ANDAs[68](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=68)[69](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=69)[70](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=70)[71](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=71) .
- Icosapent Ethyl (Vascepa): FDA told Teva (ANDA 209525) it "may be eligible for 180 days of shared" exclusivity as one of the first applicants[57](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=57) .


For contrast, some recent first-generic grants sit with a single named holder, at least as reflected in the current PC listings, including Topiramate (Alkem, ANDA 217795, exclusivity to 2026-01-05)[62](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=62) , Perampanel (MSN, ANDA 218152)[66](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=66) , Liraglutide (Teva, ANDA 214568)[72](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=72) , Ipratropium Bromide inhalation (Armstrong, ANDA 217953)[73](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=73) , Bosutinib (Alembic, ANDA 209543)[88](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=88) , Bosentan (Natco, ANDA 213154)[89](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=89) , and injectable Acetaminophen (Baxter, ANDA 214331)[91](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=91) .


### What the recent record tells regulatory and IP strategists


Three themes emerge from the recent approvals. First, first-to-file is necessary but far from sufficient. The recurring 30-month tentative-approval forfeiture finding means the value of the exclusivity is captured only by applicants whose CMC, bioequivalence, and labeling packages are clean enough to earn tentative approval promptly, and forfeiture analysis is a routine, product-specific part of every first-generic approval decision[9](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=9)[29](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=29)[32](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=32)[43](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=43) .


Second, the economics of the reward are being diluted by shared exclusivity. When ten or more companies file substantially complete Paragraph IV ANDAs on the same first day, as in dapagliflozin, the 180 days are shared across the entire cohort and any eligible ANDA can launch, which sharply compresses the head start any single first applicant enjoys[76](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=76)[79](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=79)[80](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=80)[81](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=81)[82](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=82)[83](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=83)[84](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=84)[85](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=85)[86](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=86)[87](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=87) .


Third, forfeiture is adjudicated, not mechanical. FDA has declined to find forfeiture where a missed 30-month deadline was caused by changed approval requirements, so applicants that miss the window on grounds outside their control should preserve and present that causation argument[37](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=37)[38](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=38)[12](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-180-day-generic-exclusivity-how-it-works?showSourceNumber=12) .


A natural follow-up for a specific molecule is to pull the individual ANDA approval letter and 180-day exclusivity memo to see FDA's exact first-applicant determination, the forfeiture analysis, and the triggering-event calculation, which is where the fact-specific reasoning lives.
